content:
I discovered a feature hidden in the System Settings app today that I never knew existed: you can set different default languages for individual Mac apps. If you already knew this, there's nothing to see, move along. But if not, I'll explain how this feature works (and how it doesn't)...

Today, many people are bilingual and have to switch between languages throughout the day depending on the audience and context. Personally, I don't really have this problem, but I do constantly find myself switching between British English (i.e., English...) and American English.

(Just to be clear, this line is just a joke! Some British English usages are actually preserved from American English and only changed later, such as the suffix -ize becoming -ise in British English. Incidentally, as James Nicoll said: "The problem with defending the purity of the English language is that the purity of English is about the same as the purity of a brothel. Not only does English borrow words, it occasionally chases other languages down an alley to beat them up and rifled through their pockets for new vocabulary.")

Switching between two languages means I can't rely on spell check to catch cases where the word is correct but uses the other version of English. I always thought this had to be handled manually, but today I discovered at least one partial workaround.

At the bottom of System Preferences > General > Language & Region, there's an 'Applications' section tucked away. You can add apps and select a language. The fact that British English is called 'English (UK)' while American English is simply called 'English – English' reveals Apple's US-centric bias.

In my case, I do most of my writing in the browser, so I use two different browsers depending on the target language. I set British English as the system language, so Safari uses British English, while I set Chrome (alphabetically listed as Google Chrome) to use American English.

As I discovered, there's an important caveat here: only apps that support macOS localisation/language APIs can be configured this way, so not all apps will appear in the list.

If I'm the last person on Earth to discover this, feel free to look down on me with your multilingual eyes in the comments.
